newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Lili headed for Cuba, Florida, Yucatan.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Lili headed for Cuba, Florida, Yucatan.

text.p: Tropical Storm Lili churned in the northwest Caribbean Wednesday, posing a threat to Cuba, the Yucatan Peninsula and the Florida Keys, National Hurricane Center said.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, the center of Lili was near latitude 18.4 north and longitude 83.8 west, or about 345 miles (555 km) south-southwest of Havana.

Forecasters said the storm appeared to be strengthening and could become a hurricane later Wednesday. The storm was moving north at about eight mph (13 kph). Maximum sustained winds were near 50 mph (80 kph).

Cuba's government issued a hurricane watch for western Cuba and the Isle of Youth and the mainland provinces of Pinar del Rio and Havana. The hurricane center said this watch would likely be upgraded to a hurricane warning later on Wednesday.
Mexico issued a tropical storm warning along the east coast of Yucatan from Cabo Catoche south to Bahia de Chetumal, according to the hurricane center.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for the Cayman Islands, and the hurricane center also said a hurricane watch was likely to be issued for the Florida Keys later Wednesday.
Lili would become a hurricane if its maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
